_link.title: I can define torque and calculate it using τ = rF

toLevel2.stem: What is the SI unit of torque?
distractors: Newton per metre (N/m)
Kilogram metre (kg m)
Joule per second (J/s)
τ = F/r
τ = r/F
τ = r²F

toLevel2.stem: In the formula τ = rF, what does the variable r represent?
toLevel2.answer: The perpendicular distance from the pivot to the line of action of the force
distractors: The radius of the object that is rotating about the central pivot point
The total length of the lever arm measured from one end to the other end
The distance the object travels during one complete revolution of the system

toLevel2.stem: What is the torque produced by a 5.0 N force applied 0.40 m from a pivot?
What is the best definition of torque?
toLevel2.answer: The turning effect of a force about a pivot
distractors: The total force applied to a rotating object
The speed at which an object rotates freely
The energy stored in a rotating body system

toLevel2.stem: Torque is calculated by multiplying the {{blank:1}} by the perpendicular {{blank:2}} from the pivot.
The SI unit of torque is the {{blank:1}} {{blank:2}}.
Torque describes the {{blank:1}} effect of a force about a {{blank:2}} point.
Torque depends on both the magnitude of the force and the distance from the pivot.
distractors: False

toLevel2.stem: The SI unit of torque is the joule (J).
distractors: True

toLevel3.stem: Why does the same force produce less torque when applied closer to the pivot?
toLevel3.answer: Because torque is proportional to the distance from the pivot
distractors: Because the force becomes weaker when applied near the pivot
Because friction increases when the force is near the pivot
Because the mass of the lever increases closer to the pivot

toLevel3.stem: A force of 8.0 N is applied at 0.25 m from a pivot. What force applied at 0.50 m would produce the same torque?
Why is r in τ = rF specifically the perpendicular distance, not just any distance from the pivot?
toLevel3.answer: Only the perpendicular component of the distance contributes to the turning effect
distractors: The parallel component of distance doubles the effective turning force value
Perpendicular distance is easier to measure than the actual distance value
Any distance from the pivot gives the same torque regardless of its angle

toLevel3.stem: A student doubles both the force and the distance from the pivot. By what factor does the torque change?
toLevel3.answer: It increases by a factor of four
distractors: It increases by a factor of two
It stays exactly the same value
It increases by a factor of eight

toLevel3.stem: In a DC motor, why does a wider coil produce more torque than a narrower coil for the same force?
toLevel3.answer: The forces act at a greater distance from the axis of rotation
distractors: A wider coil carries a larger current through its conducting wires
A wider coil has a stronger magnetic field inside its interior area
A wider coil has less electrical resistance in its conducting wires

toLevel3.stem: Which pair of values would produce a torque of 6.0 N m?
toLevel3.answer: A force of 20 N at a distance of 0.30 m
distractors: A force of 20 N at a distance of 0.60 m
A force of 30 N at a distance of 0.30 m
A force of 12 N at a distance of 0.25 m

toLevel3.stem: Doubling the distance from the pivot while keeping the force constant will {{blank:1}} the torque by a factor of {{blank:2}}.
In a DC motor, the torque on the coil depends on the {{blank:1}} on each side and the {{blank:2}} of the coil.
If a force is not perpendicular to the lever arm, only the {{blank:1}} component of the force contributes to the {{blank:2}}.
Applying a larger force at the same distance from the pivot always produces a larger torque.
distractors: False

toLevel4.stem: A motor coil has sides 0.08 m from the axis. Each side experiences a force of 0.50 N. What is the total torque on the coil?
A spanner 0.25 m long is used to turn a bolt. If the maximum force a person can apply is 60 N, what is the maximum torque they can exert?
distractors: 240 N m
7.5 N m

toLevel4.stem: A motor coil is oriented so the plane of the coil makes an angle of 90° with the magnetic field. What can be said about the torque at this position?
toLevel4.answer: The torque is zero because the forces act through the axis of rotation
distractors: The torque is at its maximum because the forces are at their strongest
The torque is zero because no force acts on the coil at this position
The torque is at half its maximum value at this particular orientation

toLevel4.stem: A force of 12 N is applied to a lever arm at 30° to the perpendicular. If the lever arm is 0.40 m, what is the effective torque?
distractors: 4.8 N m
2.4 N m
1.2 N m

toLevel4.stem: Two forces of equal magnitude act on opposite sides of a motor coil. Why do they produce a net torque rather than cancelling out?
toLevel4.answer: They act in opposite directions on opposite sides, both contributing to rotation in the same sense
distractors: They act in the same direction and add together to create a larger linear force
One force is always larger than the other due to the variation in the field strength
They cancel the linear motion but create a sideways push on the coil axle instead

toLevel4.stem: A motor designer wants to double the torque without changing the current or magnetic field. Which modification would achieve this?
toLevel4.answer: Double the width of the coil
distractors: Double the length of the coil
Halve the width of the coil
Double the mass of the coil

toLevel4.stem: A student calculates a torque of 4.5 N m using a force of 15 N. What distance from the pivot was the force applied?
In a motor, both sides of the coil experience forces that create torques in the {{blank:1}} rotational direction, so the total torque is the {{blank:2}} of the individual torques.
When the coil plane is parallel to the field, the perpendicular distance from the axis to each force is {{blank:1}}, producing {{blank:2}} torque.
A force of 25 N applied {{blank:1}} m from a pivot produces a torque of {{blank:2}} N m.

toLevel5.stem: A student states that torque and energy have the same units and are therefore the same quantity. Evaluate this claim.
toLevel5.answer: Incorrect; although both have units of N m, torque is a rotational effect while energy is a scalar capacity to do work
distractors: Correct; torque and energy are identical quantities measured in exactly the same units
Incorrect; torque is measured in N m but energy is measured in kg m² s⁻² which differs
Correct; torque can always be directly converted into an equivalent amount of energy

toLevel5.stem: Two students debate whether a longer or shorter spanner is better for loosening a tight bolt. Which analysis is most accurate?
toLevel5.answer: A longer spanner requires less force to produce the same torque needed to loosen the bolt
distractors: A shorter spanner is better because the force is more concentrated near the bolt head
Spanner length does not matter because only the applied force determines the outcome
A longer spanner produces less torque because the force is spread over a greater area

toLevel5.stem: In a motor, the torque varies as the coil rotates. At which orientation is the torque maximum, and why?
toLevel5.answer: When the coil plane is parallel to the field, because the perpendicular distance from the axis to each force is greatest
distractors: When the coil plane is perpendicular to the field, because the force on each side is greatest
When the coil is at 45° to the field, because force and distance are equally balanced
When the coil plane is parallel to the field, because the magnetic flux is at its maximum

toLevel5.stem: A motor coil has dimensions 0.06 m × 0.04 m in a 0.20 T field carrying 3.0 A. Calculate the maximum torque on the coil.
A student claims that increasing the number of turns in a motor coil increases the torque. Analyse why this is correct.
toLevel5.answer: Each turn experiences the same force, so more turns multiply the total force and hence the torque
distractors: More turns increase the magnetic field strength which increases the perpendicular distance
More turns reduce the resistance which increases the distance from the axis of rotation
More turns increase the area of the coil which directly increases the distance to pivot

toLevel5.stem: Compare the torque on a motor coil at 0° (plane parallel to field) and at 60° from parallel. If maximum torque is τ₀, what is the torque at 60°?
An engineer needs a motor with at least 0.50 N m of torque. The coil width is 0.05 m and each side experiences 4.0 N. How many turns are needed at minimum?
distractors: 2 turns
5 turns
25 turns

toLevel5.stem: Why is it important to distinguish between the force on a motor coil and the torque it produces?
toLevel5.answer: The same force can produce different torques depending on the coil's orientation relative to the field
distractors: Force and torque are always proportional so distinguishing between them is not necessary
Torque is always larger than force so engineers must use torque to avoid damaging motors
Force acts only when the motor is stationary while torque acts only when it is spinning

toLevel5.stem: Although torque and energy share the same {{blank:1}}, torque is a measure of {{blank:2}} effect, not stored energy.
Maximum torque occurs when the coil plane is {{blank:1}} to the field because the lever arm distance is at its {{blank:2}} value.
